messages.text: Fictional Alex asks: why does the sky look blue? Explain it simply.

Sunlight looks white, but it contains all the colors of the rainbow. As it passes through the air, tiny gas molecules scatter the blue light more than most other colors, sending it in many directions. That scattered blue light reaches your eyes from all across the sky, making it look blue.
Now explain that to a ten-year-old in two sentences.
Sunlight contains all the colors of the rainbow, even though it looks white. Air scatters blue light more than most other colors, sending it all around the sky and making the sky look blue.
